list.name: namespace
list.label: Instance
list.description: The instance this board reads. Empty on purpose: the chart's templates/grafana-dashboard.yaml replaces this entry with a hidden constant naming the instance it installs, so every namespace="$namespace" selector reads that instance's series and no other. There is no instance picker: each instance ships its own copy of this board, in its own Grafana folder.

list.name: instance
list.label: Instance ID
list.description: The instance ID, used to select this instance's alerts. Empty on purpose: the chart's templates/grafana-dashboard.yaml replaces this entry with a hidden constant holding the ID of the instance it installs.

title: DeviceChain — Delivery
description: Operations board for everything the platform sends out other than commands: outbound connectors (webhooks and message publishing), alarm notifications and their escalation, and over-the-air software updates, plus the hand-off from automation rules. Connectors and software updates are optional areas; their rows stay empty on an install without them. Commands have their own board.

panels.title: Firing alerts
panels.description: Alerts firing right now for this instance that concern outbound delivery: connector dispatches refused for rate, and automation actions held back at the source for being over a tenant's outbound limit. An empty table means none are firing. Alerts come from the instance's Prometheus rules, so the table stays empty if those rules are not installed. Notifications and software updates have no alerts of their own yet.

panels.title: Sent /s
panels.description: Reports only when the outbound connectors area is installed (it is optional and not part of the default install). Without it this panel stays empty. Webhook calls and published messages that reached their destination, per second. Zero is normal when no rule is sending anything out.

panels.title: Retrying /s
panels.description: Reports only when the outbound connectors area is installed (it is optional and not part of the default install). Without it this panel stays empty. Sends that failed for a reason that may pass (destination error, non-success reply, a brief secret-store problem) and were left to be tried again. A steady rate means a destination is unhealthy; check the destination first.

panels.title: Given up on
panels.description: Reports only when the outbound connectors area is installed (it is optional and not part of the default install). Without it this panel stays empty. Dispatches set aside as dead letters over the selected time range, for any reason: failed after every retry, malformed, unsupported connector type, blocked destination, or over the rate limit. One is enough to look. List them with `dcctl dead-letters` and read the reason on each.

panels.title: Blocked destinations
panels.description: Reports only when the outbound connectors area is installed (it is optional and not part of the default install). Without it this panel stays empty. Dispatches refused over the selected time range because the destination resolved to an address a tenant may not reach (private, loopback, link-local or cloud metadata). Fix the connector's address; retrying never helps.

panels.title: Lost dispatches
panels.description: Reports only when the outbound connectors area is installed (it is optional and not part of the default install). Without it this panel stays empty. Dispatches over the selected time range that could be neither sent nor recorded as a dead letter, because the dead-letter write itself failed. These are lost. Check that the message broker is healthy.

panels.title: Waiting to be sent
panels.description: Reports only when the outbound connectors area is installed (it is optional and not part of the default install). Without it this panel stays empty. Dispatch requests the connectors service has not been handed yet, as last sampled. A number that keeps growing means sends are not keeping up; look at the retry and given-up panels below.

panels.title: Dispatches by outcome
panels.description: Reports only when the outbound connectors area is installed (it is optional and not part of the default install). Without it this panel stays empty. Every dispatch handled, by how it ended: sent, retry (will be tried again), dead (gave up after the retry limit), invalid, unsupported, blocked, rate_limited, tenant_deleted (dropped on purpose), dead_write_failed, dead_index_failed. A healthy install is almost all sent.

panels.title: Sent by connector type
panels.description: Reports only when the outbound connectors area is installed (it is optional and not part of the default install). Without it this panel stays empty. Successful sends split by what the rule asked for: httpCall (a webhook) or publish (a message to a broker). Sends are not split by individual connector or by tenant.

panels.title: Failures by connector type and reason
panels.description: Reports only when the outbound connectors area is installed (it is optional and not part of the default install). Without it this panel stays empty. Dispatches that were retried or given up on, by connector type and outcome. Retries are temporary and clear on their own; given-up outcomes are in the dead-letter list. A rise in rate_limited usually means the connectors service and the automation engine disagree about a tenant's outbound limit.

panels.title: Dispatch backlog
panels.description: Reports only when the outbound connectors area is installed (it is optional and not part of the default install). Without it this panel stays empty. Requests waiting for the connectors service (not yet handed over) and requests handed over but not yet confirmed, as last sampled every 30 seconds. Both should sit near zero.

panels.title: Actions handed to each sink
panels.description: Automation-rule actions handed on for delivery, by action type (raiseAlarm, sendCommand, httpCall, publish and so on), as counted by the rule engine. Compare httpCall and publish with the connector panels above: the engine's count should be close to what the connectors service handles. A gap means the connectors service is missing, down, or behind. Detail is on the event processing board.

panels.title: Actions that could not be carried out
panels.description: Actions the rule engine did not hand on, by cause: recognised but no service installed to carry them out (not enabled, for example a webhook with no connectors area), refused for good by the receiving service (permanently rejected, an authoring mistake such as a command the device cannot accept), or skipped before an attempt (dropped). Fix the rule or install the missing area.

panels.title: Connector actions held back for being over quota
panels.description: Webhook and publish actions the rule engine refused to send because the tenant was over its outbound calls limit, per second, split by how they were recorded: as an individual dead letter, or counted and summarised once a minute because the recording budget ran out. The first alert above fires on sustained shedding. Raise the tenant's outbound limits if the traffic is legitimate.

panels.title: Rule results set aside after retries
panels.description: Rule results the engine gave up on after the retry limit (dead lettered) and results whose rule no longer exists (orphaned). Dead-lettered results can be inspected with `dcctl dead-letters`. A steady rate means an action keeps failing for a reason a retry cannot fix.

panels.title: Handled /s
panels.description: Alarm notifications the notification service finished handling per second. Zero is normal when no alarms are changing state.

panels.title: Retrying /s
panels.description: Notifications that failed on this attempt and were left to be tried again, per second. A steady rate points at a channel (mail relay or webhook) that is failing.

panels.title: Never delivered
panels.description: Notifications over the selected time range that every attempt failed to deliver and that were set aside as dead letters, so the page was never sent. One is enough to look: `dcctl dead-letters` lists them.

panels.title: Refused deliveries
panels.description: Channel deliveries over the selected time range that were refused on the first attempt and not retried: the destination is not one outbound traffic may reach, a required credential is missing, or the channel type is not available in this build. The reasons are charted below. Fix the channel's settings.

panels.title: Held by quiet hours
panels.description: Notifications deferred by a policy's quiet hours over the selected time range. Informational: these are sent when the quiet stretch ends, unless the alarm is resolved first.

panels.title: Failed escalation passes
panels.description: Escalation passes over the selected time range that failed. The scheduler re-notifies alarms that stayed open; a failed pass means some of them were not re-notified until the next pass. Check the notification service log.

panels.title: Notifications by result
panels.description: Every notification attempt, by result: ok, retry (tried again later), failed (set aside as a dead letter), invalid, dropped, erased. A healthy install is almost all ok.

panels.title: Time to handle a notification
panels.description: How long the notification service took to handle one notification, including contacting the mail relay or webhook. Slow handling usually means a slow destination. Not split by channel type.

panels.title: Refusals and quiet hours
panels.description: Refused deliveries by reason (egress: destination not reachable by policy; credential: a required credential is missing or an unexpected one is stored; no_adapter: channel type unavailable), and notifications affected by quiet hours by outcome (held, released, and the reasons a held one was dropped).

panels.title: Escalation passes
panels.description: Passes of the escalation scheduler, by outcome. It runs on a timer in every replica of the notification service. Failed passes need attention; skipped means another replica held the work.

panels.title: Notification backlog
panels.description: Alarm events waiting for the notification service and events handed over but not yet confirmed, as last sampled every 30 seconds. Both should sit near zero; a growing number means notifications are late.

panels.title: Device reports /s
panels.description: Reports only when the software update area is installed (it ships in the full install, not the default one). Without it this panel stays empty. Progress and inventory reports devices sent about updates, per second, whatever the outcome.

panels.title: Reports not applied /s
panels.description: Reports only when the software update area is installed (it ships in the full install, not the default one). Without it this panel stays empty. Device reports the update state machine did not apply (duplicate, stale, wrong checksum, regression and so on), per second. A rising rate from one fleet is usually a device-side bug; see the breakdown below.

panels.title: Download traffic
panels.description: Reports only when the software update area is installed (it ships in the full install, not the default one). Without it this panel stays empty. Artifact bytes streamed to devices per second.

panels.title: Downloads refused
panels.description: Reports only when the software update area is installed (it ships in the full install, not the default one). Without it this panel stays empty. Download requests over the selected time range that were refused or cut short (anything other than served). A rise in invalid capabilities means someone is guessing download links.

panels.title: Failed rollout steps
panels.description: Reports only when the software update area is installed (it ships in the full install, not the default one). Without it this panel stays empty. Rollout steps over the selected time range that failed and were left for the next pass. A steady rise means rollouts are not advancing: device management unreachable, or a database error.

panels.title: Updates not pushed to devices
panels.description: Reports only when the software update area is installed (it ships in the full install, not the default one). Without it this panel stays empty. Assignments, download grants and cancels over the selected time range that could not be put on a device's desired channel. The device picks the state up at its next sync, so this is a delay rather than a loss.

panels.title: Device reports by verdict
panels.description: Reports only when the software update area is installed (it ships in the full install, not the default one). Without it this panel stays empty. Reports by the verdict the update state machine gave: APPLIED, or the reason it was not.

panels.title: Reports refused before applying
panels.description: Reports only when the software update area is installed (it ships in the full install, not the default one). Without it this panel stays empty. Device messages refused before reaching the state machine, by reason: malformed, unattributable, throttled (a sync inside the per-device cooldown) or device_disabled.

panels.title: Downloads by result
panels.description: Reports only when the software update area is installed (it ships in the full install, not the default one). Without it this panel stays empty. Artifact download requests by result: served, aborted, or why one was refused. A high busy count means the download limit is too low for the fleet.

panels.title: Download grants by result
panels.description: Reports only when the software update area is installed (it ships in the full install, not the default one). Without it this panel stays empty. Download permissions requested by devices, by outcome: granted, or why the assignment could not be downloaded. not_configured means the download base address is unset and no device can download.

panels.title: Rollout progress
panels.description: Reports only when the software update area is installed (it ships in the full install, not the default one). Without it this panel stays empty. Devices a group rollout decided (dispatched or skipped) and rollouts that moved on their own (completed, or paused because the failure limit was reached or the artifact stopped being assignable). A paused rollout needs an operator.

panels.title: Update attempts that went quiet
panels.description: Reports only when the software update area is installed (it ships in the full install, not the default one). Without it this panel stays empty. Update attempts the deadline sweep moved because the device stopped reporting: timed_out before installation started, or unknown during installation or reboot.

panels.title: Update report backlog
panels.description: Reports only when the software update area is installed (it ships in the full install, not the default one). Without it this panel stays empty. Device reports and device roster changes waiting for the update service, and ones handed over but not yet confirmed, as last sampled every 30 seconds.
